title: Two chemicals that make animal patterns
lede: The Gray-Scott model: chemical U is fed in, chemical V eats U and decays, and both spread out, V more slowly. Pick a pattern, press Reset, or drag on the picture to add V.
notice: Nothing in the rules mentions spots or stripes. They appear because V spreads more slowly than U, which Alan Turing showed can break a uniform state.
Only the feed rate F and kill rate k differ between the patterns. Small changes give spots, worms, splitting blobs or coral.
Dragging adds a patch of V. Where it lands, the pattern grows around it.
hint: Drag on the picture to add chemical V. Reset starts again.
